## How to add a comment to an IP address on VirusTotal

### 1. Prepare your request

**Endpoint**

```
POST https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments
```

**Headers**

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `x-apikey` | `ABC321` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

**Body**

```json
{
  "type": "comment",
  "attributes": {
    "text": "Confirmed #malware"
  }
}
```

> **Note:**  
> - Replace `ABC321` with your actual API key.  
> - The IP address (`192.168.1.1`) is part of the URL path.  
> - The body follows the JSON schema expected by VirusTotal for comments.

### 2. Send the request

You can send this request with any HTTP client:

- **cURL**

  ```bash
  curl -X POST \
       -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
       -d '{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}' \
       https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments
  ```

- **Python (requests)**

  ```python
  import requests

  url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments"
  headers = {
      "x-apikey": "ABC321",
      "Content-Type": "application/json"
  }
  data = {
      "type": "comment",
      "attributes": {
          "text": "Confirmed #malware"
      }
  }

  response = requests.post(url, json=data, headers=headers)
  print(response.status_code)
  print(response.json())
  ```

### 3. Check the response

A successful request will return a `201 Created` status code and a JSON object containing details about the newly created comment. If there’s an error (e.g., invalid API key, rate limit exceeded), you’ll receive an appropriate error message.
